canonical_name: Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem (ergodic, real-valued form)
canonical_statement: On a probability space with an ergodic measure-preserving transformation T, an integrable real subadditive process X satisfying X_(m+n) <= X_m + X_n after T^m and a finite lower bound on normalized expectations has X_n/n converging almost everywhere to the constant inf_{n>=1} E[X_n]/n.
domain_and_universes: Omega : Type u with MeasurableSpace Omega; probability measure mu; T : Omega -> Omega; X : Nat -> Omega -> Real
quantifiers: m n : Nat in the cocycle law
hypotheses: T is ergodic and hence measure preserving
X_(m+n) <= X_m + X_n composed with T^m almost everywhere
conclusion: X_n(omega)/n converges almost everywhere to the constant infimum of normalized expectations; the selected limit is T-invariant almost everywhere
